newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche almost quadruples half-year profits.
newsitem.headline: Porsche almost quadruples half-year profits.

text.p: Porsche AG said Friday that robust demand for its new Boxster model and the continued popularity of its famed 911 sports car enabled it to almost quadruple its net income in the first half of its fiscal year.
Porsche said its net profit soared to 38.4 million marks ($22.7 million) as sales jumped 26 percent to 1.78 billion marks ($1.05 billion).
Unit car sales climbed even faster, up 32.7 percent to 13,549 vehicles, during the six months ended Jan 31.
The company said the strong sales growth was primarily due to Porsche's new two-seat cabriolet Boxster model, which was first introduced last fall.
It added that the plant producing Boxsters, which has a capacity of around 30,000 cars a year, had been unable to keep up with demand for the model, which now has an order backlog of nearly a year.
Porsche also said the 911 model, now more than 30 years old, continued to sell well, thanks to continued upgrades that have left it one of the most advanced sports cars on the road.
